title: Homepage journeys by implementation style
content:
Purpose:
This brief experiments with hero and opening copy that map directly to a developer or buyer’s chosen implementation style (Hosted API, Dedicated/Reserved, Private deployment). Goal: reduce cognitive friction on first visit by surfacing the most relevant value path within one scroll and enable faster funnel qualification.

Target outcomes:
- Increase click-through on relevant CTAs (Get started / Contact sales / Request private trial) by 12% from baseline within 6 weeks.
- Reduce homepage bounce for mid-market engineering visitors by 8%.
- Gather variant-level qualitative feedback from 50 visitor sessions and 3 customer interviews.

Audience slices (prioritized):
1) Product/ML engineers at AI-native startups evaluating time-to-value and iteration speed.
   - Pain: getting something working quickly without losing performance.
   - Decision metric: API ergonomics, latency, sample code.
2) Platform/infra teams at mid-market companies assessing cost predictability and operational controls.
   - Pain: unpredictable token costs and noisy endpoints.
   - Decision metric: dedicated capacity, autoscaling, cost per token forecasts.
3) Security/compliance buyers at regulated enterprises who need private control planes.
   - Pain: data egress, auditability, and key management.
   - Decision metric: VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM integrations, SLAs.

Implementation-style homepage model (single page, split by quick selector):
- Top nav includes a small toggle: "I want to: [Prototype / Scale predictably / Keep data private]" (defaults to Prototype).
- Hero adapts copy and CTA based on selected path; rest of the fold shows one-line proof points tailored to the path.
- Modular underneath: 3 horizontal cards (Aligned to the 3 paths) that expand to short feature lists and one-sentence customer proof.

Hero copy variants (by path) — short and punchy:
A. Prototype (Hosted API)
  - Headline: "Ship LLM features fast — no infra headaches."
  - Subhead: "A single API for chat, generation, embeddings and streaming so your product moves from idea to demo in hours, not weeks."
  - Primary CTA: "Start free — get API keys"
  - Support bullets: "Instant models, sample prompts, SDKs in JS/Python"

B. Scale (Dedicated)
  - Headline: "Predictable throughput. Lower unit cost."
  - Subhead: "Reserved GPU capacity and autoscaling policies so latency and cost stay stable at production scale."
  - Primary CTA: "Explore Dedicated plans"
  - Support bullets: "Commit pricing, SLA-backed latency, burst capacity"

C. Private (VPC / On‑prem)
  - Headline: "Inference inside your network. Compliance-first."
  - Subhead: "Private control plane, customer-managed networking and KMS integrations for regulated workloads."
  - Primary CTA: "Request a private trial"
  - Support bullets: "Audit logs, HSM/KMS, air-gapped option"

Cross-cutting microcopy alternatives (for A/B test):
- Variant X: emphasize "cost per 1k tokens" in a short inline stat for Scale path.
- Variant Y: emphasize "time to first token" (minutes) for Prototype path.
- Variant Z: emphasize "certifications & SOC" for Private path.

Product page snippets (to slot under each card):
- Hosted API product blurb: "Start with a single REST endpoint and SDKs. Stream responses, call tools, and get structured outputs — with transparent latency metrics so you can tune for production."
- Dedicated product blurb: "Pin model versions, set autoscale windows, and get predictable tail latencies. Choose GPU class and reserve capacity to match your traffic profile."
- Private product blurb: "Run Redwood in your VPC or on-prem with a private control plane. Integrate with your identity provider, KMS, and SIEM for full auditability."

Differentiation hooks to weave in (avoid generic terms):
- "Model and kernel pairing": highlight runtime that selects optimized kernels for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- "Workload-aware batching": frame as an automatic savings lever that doesn’t require dev changes.
- "Fallback routing by policy": call out resilience — fallback to smaller-compatible variant when capacity constrained.

Social proof and proof metrics (concise):
- Inline stat examples: "<company> cut inference bill by 37% using Redwood Optimize"; "99.95% uptime on Dedicated clusters (last 90 days)"; "Avg P95 generation latency 120ms for common web seq lengths".
- Short logos row under hero (keep logos to customer-approved names only).

CTAs and funnel mapping:
- Prototype path CTA -> Sign up (self-serve) -> Quickstart that provisions API key and sample app.
- Scale path CTA -> Request pricing / Schedule a capacity call (form with traffic profile fields).
- Private path CTA -> Contact sales / Request architecture review (book a call).

A/B hypotheses and measurement plan:
- H1: Adaptive hero (selector-based) will increase CTA relevance clicks by +15% vs static hero. Metric: CTA clicks per path / sessions where path clicked.
- H2: Time-to-first-token stat increases signups from Prototype by 10%. Metric: signup conversion from hero.
- H3: Adding a cost-savings micro-stat for Scale path reduces sales discovery meetings that are price-shoppers by 20% (measure by form answer "budget" field).
- Data plan: Capture variant, path selected, CTA clicked, utm_source, time-on-page. Run stats on a 4-week rolling window with >1k sessions per variant for significance.

SEO & headline permutations to include in metadata: 
- Primary keywords: "LLM inference platform", "inference API", "dedicated GPU inference", "private LLM deployment"
- Secondary long tails: "reduce inference latency for chatbots", "reserve GPU capacity for LLMs", "VPC LLM hosting"

Design / layout notes for engineering handoff:
- Use client-side JS to swap hero copy quickly (no build) behind feature flag.
- Persist selector preference in localStorage for repeat visitors.
- Ensure server-side canonical remains same URL (no multiple landing pages) to avoid SEO dilution — use structured data and meta description fragments inserted dynamically.

Wireframe quick sketch (verbal):
- Row 1: Tiny selector pill + global nav
- Row 2: Hero (left: headline/subhead/CTA; right: short screenshot or latency stat card)
- Row 3: Three expandable cards (Prototype / Scale / Private)
- Row 4: Proof metrics + customer logos
- Row 5: Product feature slices and links to deeper product pages

Dependencies and follow-ups:
- Engineering: lightweight feature-flagged hero swap and selector component (Tickets: JIRA-7610, JIRA-7611).
- Growth: event mapping and analytics dashboard (Mixpanel tracking spec needed).
- Legal/PR: confirm logo permissions and customer quote approvals.

Open questions / decisions to make:
1) Do we show pricing examples in the Scale card (pros: faster qualification; cons: may scare non-qualified leads)? Recommendation: test with and without price banding.
2) How aggressive should the Private path security copy be? Need security/Audit review to certify claims around KMS/HSM.
3) Should we localize hero selector copy for EU (GDPR-forward) audiences? Might be beneficial.

Next steps (two-week plan):
- Week 1: Finalize 3 hero variants and copy microtests. Implement selector component behind feature flag (eng).
- Week 2: Launch A/B test to 30% of traffic; monitor funnel metrics and collect session replays for qualitative review.
- End of week 2: Review results, pick winner(s), and plan rollout for full audience or iterate further.

Notes and references:
- Customer interview insights attached in linked Confluence page INF-452.
- Related experiments: see repo PR #128 for previous hero experiments and copy assets.
